one_liner: Senior executive running DOE's non-M&O contracting enterprise as Head of Contracting Activity, overseeing acquisition strategy, bid protests, FAR/DEAR disputes, facilities and logistics.
fit_summary: This SES role requires demonstrated senior-level FAR acquisition leadership (TQ1) and executive leadership of subordinate organizations, including SES and GS-15 managers (TQ2). Daniel's known background is emergency-management consulting at IEM plus strong policy knowledge and people skills, and nothing on file shows contracting-officer or executive-level acquisition experience. Daniel would very likely not pass the minimum-qualifications screen or OPM QRB certification.
eligibility: Open to the public, and U.S. citizenship or nationality is required, so status and veterans' preference are not needed.
Your resume must show both TQs: senior-level FAR/agency acquisition expertise on complex, high-dollar contracts (TQ1) and executive leadership of acquisition programs across organizations (TQ2).
Your resume must show all five ECQs, including Leading People and Driving Efficiency, within two pages; separate narratives are not accepted.
No education requirement applies, but OPM's QRB must certify your executive qualifications before appointment.
The posting lists no clearance as required, but it also says one may be needed before entrance on duty; an OGE-278 financial disclosure and drug testing also apply.
strategy: Be honest with yourself first: apply only if your IEM work included real federal contract management, such as capture, proposal pricing, contract administration, or program management on large FEMA or HUD recovery contracts. Even then, expect a likely ineligible rating.
If you do apply, frame IEM experience through the government-contract lens: [contract vehicle], [dollar value], your role in [proposal/compliance/task order management], and FAR clauses you applied.
Map each TQ and ECQ to labeled, concise evidence within two pages, listing dates and hours per week for each job, because screeners will not read past page 2.
Use your policy knowledge to address ECQ 1 (rule of law, American system of government) and the duty of representing acquisition needs to congressional staff.
Apply between October 29 and November 12, 2026, and do not wait for the last day.

A better use of effort is to target entry or mid-level roles that fit you, such as FEMA or DHS program specialist (GS-9/11/12), contract specialist trainee (1102) roles, Virginia VDEM, Prince William County emergency management, or legislative staff positions.
resume_bullets: Supported [federal client, e.g., FEMA] [program] under a [$X] [contract type] contract, ensuring deliverables complied with [FAR/contract clauses] and [specific requirement].
Managed relationships with [number/type of] government stakeholders and contractor teams to resolve [issue type], achieving [result you can document].
Contributed to [proposal/task order/acquisition planning effort] valued at [$X], responsible for [specific role].
interview_questions: Describe a complex source selection or bid protest you led and the FAR provisions you relied on.
How have you driven efficiency and cut wasteful spending in an acquisition organization?
Tell us about holding a senior manager accountable during organizational change.
How would you explain DOE's acquisition priorities to skeptical congressional staff?
watch_outs: The core requirements, SES-level FAR acquisition leadership and executive supervision, are not reflected in Daniel's known background, so disqualification at minimum-qualifications review is highly likely.
The two-page resume limit is strictly enforced, and ECQs and TQs must fit inside it.
The selectee must pass OPM QRB certification, serve a one-year probationary period, and file an OGE-278 financial disclosure.
